Ingots of CoFeNiMnV HEAs were prepared by arc melting high purity Co, Fe, Ni, Mn, and V mixtures comprising pure metals (purity > 99.9 wt %) under an argon atmosphere. During the smelting process, the alloys were re-smelted at least four times to ensure their compositional homogeneity.

The as-cast ingots were encapsulated in quartz ampules, homogenised for 4 h at 1000 ◦C, and then cold-rolled (CR) at room temperature with a thickness reduction of 60 % to produce a 1.3-mm-thick sheet.

attributes.morphology: black bands in IPF images (unindexed large lattice distortion)

evidence.quote: When the samples were annealed at 700 and 800 ◦C, all or most of the deformed grains were not recrystallised, and some regions with larger lattice distortions were beyond the resolution limit required for EBSD indexing, shown as black bands in the IPF images (Fig. 3a and b).
In the 700A sample, a high density of dislocations was concentrated within or along the deformed grains without recrystallisation (Fig. 3a1).

attributes.morphology: small number of recrystallized grains in shear regions with high KAM

evidence.quote: With an increase in the annealing temperature, a small number of recrystallised grains in the 800A sample were produced in the shear regions with high KAM values (Fig. 3b1), suggesting that partial recrystallisation occurred.
For the sample annealed at 900 ◦C, the IPF map exhibited a microstructure with partial recrystallisation (Fig. 3c).
When the annealing temperature increased to 1000 ◦C, the deformed microstructure was completely replaced by refined equiaxed recrystallised grains (Fig. 3d).
